note:
Cross-reference at filing time: sibling #2432 (proposed) is the ADJACENT but DISTINCT defect.

- #2432 — the Step 10d per-leg lint fence is 900s while the work measures
  799-1085s, so healthy gates get killed (rc=124) by load rather than by the
  branch under test. That is the DEFECT.
- #2458 (this task) — the crash arm computes GT_RC / BASE_RC / GATED_RC /
  TG_RC / TG_BASE_RC / TG_CRASH, branches on them, and persists none, so a
  `crash` verdict names no cause. That is its DETECTABILITY.

They are worth fixing together but neither subsumes the other: raising the
fence removes today's dominant crash source while leaving every future crash
equally opaque.

Corroboration that the observability gap has its own cost: #2432's body records
that this same missing telemetry produced an INVERTED reading during #2217 (the
buffered-stdout/unbuffered-stderr split makes a fence-killed leg 1 look like a
passing leg 1 plus a silent leg 2). #2241 independently hit the identical
inversion on 2026-08-21 and spent a full forensic pass — ten artifact files plus
three live re-probes — before #2432's filing-time advisory surfaced the answer.
Two issues, same wrong first reading, same root: the rc is never written down.

#2241's own relaunch carries the proposed fix ad hoc (six echoes: one per lint
leg, one after mapped-baseline, one summary before the verdict `if`), so a
working shape already exists to lift into the spec.
